sources.citation: SEER Cancer Statistics: Liver and Intrahepatic Bile Duct Cancer 2018-2023
Hepatocellular Carcinoma Incidence and Mortality in the USA

metadata.description: 10-year risk of hepatocellular carcinoma and other liver cancers

caseFatality10yr.basis: SEER 5-year relative survival 21.9% (all stages, 2016-2022) -> CFR 0.781; relative survival nets out background mortality (10-year survival is modestly lower, so this is a slight underestimate)
caseFatality10yr.citation: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, National Cancer Institute

curves.source: Derived from the unstratified curve using age-specific male:female HCC incidence ratios (Liu P, et al. Age-specific sex difference in the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in the United States. Oncotarget. 2017;8(40):68131-68137, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.19245: ratio ~1.6 under 30, peak 5.40 at 50-54, ~2.5 at 80-84; SEER liver+IBD age-adjusted male 13.9 vs female 5.7 per 100k)
curves.notes: male = c*2r/(1+r), female = c*2/(1+r) with age-interpolated ratio r

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence; strongly associated with viral hepatitis

riskFactors.name: Hepatitis B Infection
riskFactors.citation: Hepatitis B and Liver Cancer Meta-analysis
riskFactors.notes: Chronic HBV HR~15-20 for HCC; major global risk factor

riskFactors.name: Hepatitis C Infection
riskFactors.citation: Hepatitis C and Liver Cancer Meta-analysis
riskFactors.notes: Chronic HCV HR~17 for HCC; curable with direct-acting antivirals

riskFactors.name: Cirrhosis
riskFactors.citation: Sorensen HT, et al. Risk of liver and other types of cancer in patients with cirrhosis: a nationwide cohort study in Denmark. Hepatology. 1998;28(4):921-925; Bengtsson B, et al. United European Gastroenterol J. 2022
riskFactors.notes: Cirrhosis: HCC incidence 26-60x the general population (Swedish nationwide 10-yr cumulative incidence 12.2%; Danish SIR 60 for HCC). Wired to the cirrhosis condition checkbox; non-cirrhotic chronic liver disease (~3-4x) is captured via the NAFLD progression model instead.

riskFactors.name: Heavy Alcohol Consumption

mapping.notes: Heavy drinking causes cirrhosis leading to HCC

riskFactors.citation: Chuang SC, Lee YC, Wu GJ, Straif K, Hashibe M. Alcohol consumption and liver cancer risk: a meta-analysis. Cancer Causes Control. 2015;26(9):1205-1231
riskFactors.notes: Dose-response (converted at 14 g/US drink): 12 g/day -> RR 1.08; 50 g/day -> 1.54; 75 g/day -> 2.14; 100 g/day -> 3.21. Synergistic with hepatitis and diabetes.

riskFactors.name: Diabetes

mapping.notes: Diabetes increases HCC risk via NAFLD

riskFactors.citation: Diabetes mellitus and risk of hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Diabetes Metab Res Rev. 2012;28(2):109-122
riskFactors.notes: Pooled RR 2.31 (1.87-2.84); cohort-only RR 2.23 (1.68-2.96). Current value 2.0 is conservative.

riskFactors.name: Obesity (BMI)
riskFactors.citation: Chen Y, Wang X, Wang J, Yan Z, Luo J. Excess Body Mass Index and Risk of Liver Cancer: A Nonlinear Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies. PLoS One. 2012;7(9):e44522
riskFactors.notes: Nonlinear dose-response; risk rises faster in men.
